subject: Pilot technical gate: benchmark success criteria, latency/cost targets, model shortlist
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
To: Claire Johnson <claire@healthpilot.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Mar 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot - technical gate recap & proposed milestones (MAP draft)

Hi Claire — great to meet earlier today. Quick recap + a proposed technical evaluation milestone set for the Mutual Action Plan so we all have the same expectations. Keeping this tight so we can convert to MAP items.

Call recap (30m):
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference for HealthPilot triage + summarization flows at production latency and unit cost targets.
- Key success: parity on intent classification/slot extraction + stable latency under realistic load.

Proposed Technical Evaluation milestone (high level):
1) Benchmark success criteria (acceptance):
   - Intent classification accuracy >= 92% on HealthPilot test set (balanced sample).
   - Summarization quality: ROUGE-L >= 0.45 on evaluation prompts (or no regression vs current baseline).
   - Error rate under load: < 0.5% request failures.
2) Latency & cost targets:
   - p95 generation latency <= 300 ms for 256-token context (tail SLOs matter more than median).
   - p95 <= 450 ms for 512-token contexts during steady-state.
   - Cost target: unit inference cost aiming for <$0.0015 per 1k input tokens (we will produce an estimate per model).
3) Model shortlist to exercise (initial):
   - Meta Llama-2-13B-chat (4-bit quantized)
   - Mistral-Instruct-7B (int8)
   - Open-instruct large model (customer-permitted 13B/33B option)
   - Redwood-curated variant (latency-optimized)

Proposed schedule & owners:
- Mar 6: HealthPilot confirms dataset owners and provides sample dataset (Claire).
- Mar 10: Redwood provides benchmark harness, runbook, and temporary endpoints (Karthik).
- Mar 13-20: Benchmarks run and initial results out (Redwood ops + HealthPilot SMEs).
- Mar 24: Readout + acceptance decision (joint).

Dependencies / blockers we flagged on call:
- Security: HealthPilot needs SOC2 evidence and IP allowlist before giving production-like datasets.
- Network: if you prefer VPC/private deployment we may need some extra steps to provision test VPC.

Attachments: I attached a lightweight benchmark template and a MAP draft (pdf) for this milestone.

Next steps for you: please confirm the shortlist and the dataset timing by EOD Mar 6 so we can lock engineers and schedule baseline runs. Also confirm who on your side owns security approvals so we can loop in our compliance team.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
Evelyn Hart | Redwood Inference
Attachments: healthpilot-benchmark-template.xlsx (spreadsheet), map-draft-v2.pdf (MAP milestone draft)

Date: Mon, 06 Mar 2028 09:04:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Pilot - technical gate recap & proposed milestones (MAP draft)

Thanks Evelyn — this looks good and aligns with our internal priorities. A few notes / clarifications from our side: 

- Owners: I will own data delivery (Claire Johnson). Our security lead (Samir Patel, security@healthpilot.com) will own SOC2 evidence & IP allowlist requests.
- Dataset: we'll provide a 5k-row anonymized sample by EOD Mar 6. Full dataset for benchmark (50k rows) will require clearance and likely be staged to a test bucket by Mar 10 if SOC2 evidence is acceptable.
- VPC preference: we prefer a private VPC trial for the POC; can Redwood do an on-prem-like network test or provide temporary VPC endpoints?
- Model shortlist: we are okay with the first three candidates; please include a smaller 2-3B baseline so we can understand cost/latency tradeoffs.

Question: can Redwood provide an estimate of expected token-unit cost for each model ahead of the runs? We need that to line up procurement approvals.

I'll confirm the exact people who should receive the benchmark run readout (ops + ML lead).

Best,
Claire Johnson
Director of Product | HealthPilot
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Claire Johnson <claire@healthpilot.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Mar 2028 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot - technical gate recap & proposed milestones (MAP draft)

Thanks — adding a bit more technical specificity so the MAP milestone is actionable from an ops + benchmark perspective.

Bench plan (detailed):
- Datasets: HealthPilot provides two artifacts: 1) classification test set (5k sample), 2) 50k anonymized pass for throughput tests. We'll run both.
- Quality thresholds:
   * Intent classification: accuracy >= 92% (micro-average). If class imbalance exists we'll report macro as well.
   * Extraction (slots): F1 >= 0.88 on labeled subset.
   * Summarization: ROUGE-L >= 0.45 OR no regression vs your current baseline.
- Latency targets (p95):
   * 256-token context: <= 300 ms (cold start excluded — measured after warm-up window).
   * 512-token context: <= 450 ms.
- Load profile: steady-state 20 QPS sustained for 10 minutes, plus 100 QPS spike for 30s to validate tail behavior.
- Cost reporting: we'll provide cost-per-1k-input and per-1k-output tokens for each model run; target guidance (ballpark):
   * 3B class models (int8): ~$0.40 - $0.60 per 1k tokens (in-hosting estimate)
   * 13B quant (4-bit): ~$0.12 - $0.25 per 1k tokens
   * 33B or larger: higher — we'll include exact numbers after kernel selection and run profile.

Responsibilities (quick):
- Redwood: deliver benchmark harness, runbook, temporary endpoints, baseline resource (1x A100-80GB) by Mar 10. Provide instructions for telemetry collection and a template for result CSVs.
- HealthPilot: provide dataset and test prompts, approve IP allowlist, confirm if VPC is required.

Acceptance criteria & gating:
- If any model misses the quality threshold but passes latency/cost, we mark for second-pass tuning (prompt engineering + cache config).
- If latency SLO is failed for all variants, we propose a fallback model-tier map in the MAP (e.g., small model for inline low-latency, larger models for background tasks).

I'll attach the minimal run commands and a sample run YAML in the Drive folder referenced.

On timing: if Claire can get the dataset by EOD Mar 6 and we have IP allowlist by Mar 9, we can begin runs Mar 13 as proposed.

-Karthik
Principal Engineer, Deployment — Redwood Inference
